opts: Retention of the succenturiate lobe causing PPH and placenta previa
Immediate fetal phocomelia with amputation of the digits
Complete congenital heart block appearing in the newborn
Premature closure of the ductus arteriosus in the fetus
exp: Placenta succenturiata has a separate accessory lobe joined by intramembranous vessels, risking a retained succenturiate lobe with postpartum hemorrhage and an increased risk of placenta previa.

opts: Stop the oxytocin infusion and give terbutaline 0.25 mg SC for acute tocolysis
Increase the oxytocin infusion to accelerate the delivery urgently
Give an intravenous bolus of methylergometrine to contract the uterus
Give a high-dose magnesium sulfate bolus for fetal neuroprotection
exp: For acute decelerations with uterine hyperstimulation, discontinue the oxytocin infusion immediately and give terbutaline 0.25 mg SC for acute tocolysis.

opts: Offer CVS or amniocentesis for diagnosis, or secondary screening with NIPT
Reassure the patient that the fetus is entirely normal on this result
Perform an immediate emergency caesarean delivery of the fetus
Repeat exactly the same biochemical test again next week
exp: A combined first-trimester risk of 1:80 is screen positive, so offer diagnostic confirmation by CVS or amniocentesis, or secondary screening with NIPT.

opts: Rapidly dividing cytotrophoblast and mesenchyme of the chorion frondosum
Desquamated fibroblasts from the fetal dermis in the amniotic fluid
Epithelial cells shed from the amniotic membrane surface
Fetal nucleated red blood cells from the circulating blood
exp: CVS aspirates and cultures the rapidly dividing cytotrophoblast (and mesenchyme) of the chorion frondosum.

opts: It is a screening and not a diagnostic test, so positives need confirmation
Its sensitivity for Down syndrome is under 70% in practice
It carries about a 1% risk of procedure-related miscarriage
It cannot be performed at all in Rh-negative mothers
exp: The primary limitation of NIPT is that it is an advanced screening test and not definitive; positive results must be confirmed invasively.

opts: Rectal mucosa, then internal sphincter, then external sphincter end to end
External sphincter, then the rectal mucosa, then the internal sphincter
Vaginal mucosa, then the external sphincter, then the rectal mucosa
Perineal skin, then the internal sphincter, then the external sphincter
exp: Repair of a 3rd or 4th degree tear proceeds from the rectal mucosa to the internal anal sphincter, then the external anal sphincter end to end, then the rest as for an episiotomy.

opts: Preterm birth history, cervical length 2.5 cm or less on TVS, singleton
Preterm labour history, a twin pregnancy, and a short cervix
A short cervix, vaginal bleeding, and evidence of infection
A previous LSCS, a short cervix, and a singleton pregnancy
exp: Cervical circlage requires all three of: a history of preterm birth, cervical length 2.5 cm or less on TVS, and a singleton pregnancy.

opts: Large placental lacunae, also called placental lakes
The twin peak sign of a dichorionic pregnancy
A snowstorm appearance filling the uterine cavity
The ring of fire seen around a corpus luteum
exp: Large placental lacunae (placental lakes) are sonolucent areas with a moth-eaten appearance and increased vascularity on Doppler.

opts: Pulmonary hypoplasia, the most lethal complication, and limb contractures
Duodenal atresia together with macroglossia in the newborn
A complete hydatidiform mole developing in the uterus
Premature closure of the ductus arteriosus before delivery
exp: Severe early oligohydramnios is devastating because it causes pulmonary hypoplasia, the most lethal complication, and severe limb reduction contractures.

opts: The triad plus a positive UPT plus localizing signs on examination
Pruritus together with jaundice and a raised bile acid level
A positive indirect Coombs test taken on its own
A normal blood glucose test with no other clinical signs
exp: Surgical management of ectopic pregnancy is indicated directly by the triad plus a positive UPT plus localizing signs.

opts: Ultrasound evidence of fetal macrosomia before term
A pregnant woman under 24 weeks with a dilated cervix
A closed cervix at 39 weeks with a normal lie
Only a positive indirect Coombs test result
exp: Emergency cervical cerclage is based on a pregnant woman under 24 weeks with a dilated cervix.

opts: Stop all fetal monitoring, since sensitisation is inevitable
No role; manage as a sensitized Rh-negative pregnancy
Give double the routine dose of anti-D immediately
Give anti-D every day until delivery is achieved
exp: Once the indirect Coombs test is positive, anti-D has no role and the pregnancy is managed as a sensitized Rh-negative pregnancy.

opts: Any position other than 1 to 5, that is ROP 6, DOP 7 or LOP 8
Any position other than the direct occipito-anterior position
Any of the positions numbered 1 to 5 in the textbook
The lateral positions LOT and ROT only, when persistent
exp: Malposition is a longitudinal lie with cephalic presentation and vertex presenting part in any position other than 1-5, that is ROP 6, DOP 7 or LOP 8.

opts: Yes, oliguria is the very first sign of magnesium toxicity
Yes, oliguria proves that cardiac arrest is imminent
No, oliguria has no relevance at all to magnesium dosing
No; it prompts monitoring because MgSO4 is renally excreted
exp: Oliguria is not itself a sign of magnesium sulfate toxicity; it prompts monitoring because MgSO4 is excreted by the kidney.

opts: Complete perineal tear, which is why episiotomy is indicated
Shoulder dystocia, managed by the McRoberts manoeuvre
Cord prolapse, needing an immediate caesarean section
Postpartum haemorrhage, treated with oxytocin
exp: The commonest complication of face-to-pubes delivery is a complete perineal tear, which is why it is an indication for episiotomy.

opts: 7.25 or more normal; 7.20 to 7.24 pre-acidotic; under 7.20 acidotic
7.40 or more normal; 7.30 pre-acidotic; under 7.25 acidotic
7.10 or more normal; under 7.00 acidotic; nothing in between
7.00 or more is normal in every labour, whatever the trace
exp: Fetal scalp pH of 7.25 or more is normal, 7.20 to 7.24 is pre-acidotic and is repeated in 20-30 minutes, and under 7.20 is acidotic and requires immediate delivery.

opts: Instrumental delivery and perineal or vaginal tear repair; cervical tears
Caesarean section and manual removal of the placenta; episiotomy
Repair of cervical tears; repair of the perineum afterwards
Suction evacuation of the uterus; instrumental delivery in labour
exp: Pudendal block is used for instrumental delivery and repair of perineal or vaginal tears, but it does not block pain during repair of cervical tears.

opts: Intrauterine growth restriction and antepartum hemorrhage from abruption
Fetal macrosomia together with polyhydramnios in the third trimester
Down syndrome and maternal hyperthyroidism in the index pregnancy
Post-term pregnancy with a persistently high serum hCG level
exp: A circumvallate placenta shows a thick raised rolled white ring at the margin with central depression, and predisposes to IUGR and antepartum hemorrhage (abruptio placentae).

opts: At least one vertical pocket of amniotic fluid measuring 2.0 cm or more
An amniotic fluid index of 15 cm or more on the scan
A fluid pocket completely filled with fetal limbs throughout
A single fluid pocket measuring 8 cm or more in depth
exp: A score of 2 for amniotic fluid volume in the biophysical profile requires at least one vertical pocket measuring 2.0 cm or more (single deepest pocket).

opts: Fetal behavioural adaptation to hypoxemia, reducing energy and oxygen use
Complete motor paralysis of the fetal spinal cord from ischemia
Compression of the fetal brainstem by amniotic bands in utero
Maternal hypoglycaemia producing fetal lethargy and weakness
exp: Reduced fetal movements in chronic placental insufficiency reflect fetal compensatory behavioural adaptation to reduce energy and oxygen consumption in the face of hypoxemia.

opts: Release of heat-stable alkaline phosphatase from the placental syncytiotrophoblast
Obstruction of the maternal biliary ducts by the gravid uterus
Severe maternal osteomalacia from calcium loss in pregnancy
Demineralisation of the fetal bones in the third trimester
exp: Serum ALP rises two- to three-fold in the third trimester because of release of large quantities of heat-stable alkaline phosphatase from the placental syncytiotrophoblast.

opts: An open neural tube defect such as anencephaly or spina bifida aperta
Down syndrome, that is trisomy 21 of the fetus
A complete hydatidiform mole within the uterine cavity
Overestimation of the gestational age at the time of testing
exp: A pathologically elevated MSAFP is characteristically associated with an open neural tube defect (anencephaly, spina bifida aperta).

opts: Start methotrexate to suppress the puerperal endometrium
Shift back to oral hypoglycemic agents if they are needed
Start radioactive iodine ablation of the maternal thyroid
Stop all diabetic care and monitoring after delivery
exp: From day 2 after delivery in pregestational diabetes, the listed transition is back to oral hypoglycemic agents if needed.

opts: It rotates both fetal shoulders internally at the pelvic brim
It decreases the bisacromial diameter of the fetal shoulders
It straightens the sacrum and increases the space available
It increases the bony pelvic diameter by about 5 cm
exp: The McRoberts manoeuvre straightens the sacrum relative to the lumbar spine and increases the available space, without increasing the pelvic diameter.

opts: All bile acids are cleared rapidly from the maternal circulation
Fatty acid accumulates in the liver and free radicals form
Placental blood flow returns to normal once clearance starts
Fetal insulin secretion falls, improving the fetal condition
exp: When fatty-acid intermediates enter the maternal circulation with limited oxidative capacity, fatty acid accumulates in the liver and free radicals form.

opts: The manual vacuum aspiration syringe on its own
Ovum forceps or sponge-holding forceps
The Karman cannula used on its own
Hegar dilators used on their own
exp: Dilatation and evacuation is performed with ovum forceps or sponge-holding forceps.

opts: Abdominal cavity
Fallopian tube
Ovary
Cervix
exp: The most common site of ectopic pregnancy is the fallopian tube.

opts: 1 ovum with 2 sperms; an empty ovum with zygotic chromosome duplication
1 ovum with 1 sperm; 2 ova each fertilized by 1 sperm
2 ova with 2 sperms; 1 ovum fertilized by a single sperm
1 ovum with 1 sperm, in both partial and complete mole
exp: Partial mole arises from 1 ovum fertilized by 2 sperms, whereas complete mole arises from an empty ovum with duplication of the zygotic chromosomes.

opts: Increased maternal age, increased parity and smoking
Diabetes mellitus and Rh negativity of the mother
Thrombophilia and a fibroid uterus distorting the cavity
Cocaine use and blunt abdominal trauma in pregnancy
exp: Risk factors common to both placenta previa and abruptio placentae are increased maternal age, increased parity and smoking.

opts: Cryoprecipitate, fresh frozen plasma and blood transfusion
A heparin infusion given on its own throughout
Platelet transfusion given on its own throughout
Vitamin K given alone by slow intravenous injection
exp: Management of DIC includes cryoprecipitate, fresh frozen plasma and blood transfusion.

opts: Do not attempt to separate the placenta, and close the uterine incision first
Deliver the placenta manually before starting the hysterectomy
Leave the uterine incision open throughout the hysterectomy
Separate the placenta using controlled traction on the cord
exp: Two intraoperative rules for PAS caesarean hysterectomy are: make no attempt to separate or deliver the placenta, and close the uterine incision before proceeding to hysterectomy.

opts: Asymptomatic bacteriuria and bacterial vaginosis, neither routinely screened
Syphilis and HIV infection, neither routinely screened
Tuberculosis and malaria, neither routinely screened
Chlamydia and gonorrhoea, neither routinely screened
exp: Maternal infections linked to preterm labour for which no routine screening is advised are asymptomatic bacteriuria and bacterial vaginosis.

opts: I intact and C clear; M meconium-stained and B blood-stained are alerts
I intact and C clear; both codes are alerts on the chart
I inadequate and C clear; M is a normal finding here
Only C clear is recorded, and I is treated as an alert
exp: In the Labour Care Guide the amniotic fluid codes are I for intact and C for clear, while M (meconium-stained) and B (blood-stained) are alerts.

opts: 25 mcg oral or vaginal 3-6 hourly, max 6 doses; then oxytocin after a gap
50 mcg vaginally 2 hourly, max 4 doses; then caesarean section
100 mcg orally once only; then proceed to an oxytocin infusion
200 mcg vaginally 12 hourly, max 2 doses; then artificial rupture
exp: Misoprostol (PGE1) for induction is 25 mcg oral or vaginal repeated 3-6 hourly (4 hourly), to a maximum of 6 doses; if no labour after a 4 hour gap, move to oxytocin.

opts: Induction and augmentation of labour; not for AMTSL or PPH management
Postpartum hemorrhage; not recommended for induction of labour
Active management of the third stage; not for induction
Cervical ripening only; not recommended for augmentation
exp: Dinoprostone (PGE2) is used for induction and augmentation of labour, but WHO does not recommend it for AMTSL or PPH management.

opts: Least common breech overall, commonest in multigravida : commonest overall and in primigravida
Commonest breech overall : the least common breech variety
Commonest in primigravida : commonest in multigravida
Both occur with equal frequency in all parities
exp: Complete breech is the least common breech overall and the commonest in multigravida; frank breech is the commonest overall and in primigravida.

opts: Galactosemia or lactose intolerance in the baby
Maternal HIV infection in the Indian setting
Mastitis affecting one breast in the puerperium
COVID-19 infection in the mother after delivery
exp: The absolute contraindication to breastfeeding listed is galactosemia or lactose intolerance in the baby.
